# Akari product information

Last updated: 2026-10-24

## Summary

Akari is an iPhone app that brings your sleep, movement and food together in one place and explains in plain words what they mean for your day. It reads Apple Health on the iPhone and keeps what it works out right there. Akari is available in English and German.

Akari is designed to inform without judgment. It explains in calm, plain language and does not use alarmist wording to drive engagement.

## What Akari does

### Readiness, every morning

Each morning Akari reads last night against the user's own usual nights. Yesterday's food and strain count too.

### Nutrition: more than just calories

Every nutrient gets a row of its own, with its own symbol. Where there is a limit, Akari marks it.

### Snap, write or say what you ate

Users log food by typing or saying it the way they would tell someone, for example "Oats with banana and a flat white", or by taking a photo of the meal. Akari finds each food, its portion and what is in it. A barcode can be scanned as well.

### One goal is enough to start

Users pick one goal, and Akari brings together what that goal needs:

- For you: the user's highest-priority health areas, picked from their Apple Health data
- Dailies: six small things that make a day good: getting outside, moving, drinking water, eating enough, sleeping and reaching someone you like
- Sleep better: morning light, screens down in the evening, and a full night's sleep
- Move more: steps, time spent training, and active energy burned
- Eat well: calories, protein and fiber in view for balanced meals
- Lose weight: staying within a calorie budget while keeping protein, fiber, daily movement and two strength days a week in view

### Health Age

Akari also offers a Health Age, which is part of the subscription.

## Privacy

- Akari needs no account.
- Akari reads Apple Health on the iPhone and keeps the user's health data there.
- A food report leaves the iPhone on purpose, and only when the user taps Send. A food report helps Akari correct a food it matched wrongly or could not find. It contains the rating and reasons, an optional comment, what was typed or said, the matched foods with amounts and nutrients, anything unmatched, a scanned barcode if there was one, and the app's language, region and version. It does not include a name, an account, Apple Health data or location.
- A meal the user types, says or photographs is read by an AI service through Akari's server and not stored by Akari. The server passes the words, the photo if there is one, and the catalogue foods the app found as possible matches to Anthropic's Claude API, which returns what is in the meal; Akari keeps nothing of what was sent or of the answer, only daily counters that limit how many meals can be sent and expire after two days. Under Anthropic's commercial terms none of it is used to train models. A meal carries no Apple Health data and no account. Packages and nutrition labels are still read on the iPhone.
- The website counts visits without cookies: it records the page, referring site and country, and tells visitors apart only with a one-way hash that changes daily. No IP address is stored.
- Full details are in the privacy policy: https://joinakari.com/privacy/

## Pricing

Most of Akari is free: sleep, movement, vitals and goals.

Food logging, readiness and Health Age come with a subscription:

- Monthly: €4.99 a month
- Yearly: €39.99 a year (about €3.33 a month, saving 33%)

The subscription can be tried free for 14 days, with no commitment. What is free and what is in the subscription may still change before launch. During the beta, everything is free.

## Requirements

An iPhone with iOS 26 or later and Apple Health. Akari is available in English and German. A fitness tracker is optional: Akari reads any tracker that writes to Apple Health, like an Apple Watch, an Oura Ring, a Garmin watch or a Fitbit, and adds its sleep, heart rate and more.

## Availability

Akari is in a free public beta through Apple TestFlight: https://testflight.apple.com/join/wrv4aFVQ. The team is preparing the App Store release, which is coming soon.

## Medical scope

Akari explains a person's own health data and patterns. It does not diagnose or treat anything and is not a substitute for professional medical advice. People should talk to their doctor about health concerns.

## How Akari compares

People looking at Akari often look at these apps too. Akari works alongside most of them rather than replacing them.

- Apple Health: Apple's own app keeps and charts health data on the iPhone. Akari reads that same data, with the user's permission, and explains in plain words what it means for the day: readiness each morning, with sleep, movement and food in one place.
- Oura, Garmin, Fitbit and Apple Watch: trackers with their own apps. Akari is not a tracker. It reads what they write to Apple Health, so people keep the tracker they have and see its sleep, heart rate and activity next to the food they eat.
- Bevel: another iPhone app built on Apple Health data. Akari's own focus is no account, health data kept on the iPhone, each reading explained against the user's own usual days, and English and German.
- Yazio and MyFitnessPal: calorie counters and food diaries. Akari logs food by writing, saying or photographing it, gives every nutrient its own row, and shows food next to sleep and movement rather than on its own.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Akari?

Akari is an iPhone app that brings your sleep, movement and food together in one place and explains in plain words what they mean for your day.

### What does Akari cost?

Most of Akari is free. Food logging, readiness and Health Age need a subscription: €4.99 a month or €39.99 a year, with 14 days free to try and no commitment. During the beta everything is free.

### What do I need?

An iPhone with iOS 26 or later and Apple Health. Akari speaks English and German. A fitness tracker is optional: one that writes to Apple Health, like an Apple Watch or a Fitbit Air, adds sleep, heart rate and more. Without one, you can switch off what needs it and use Akari for the steps your iPhone counts and the food you log.

### Does Akari work with my Apple Watch, Oura, Garmin or Fitbit?

Yes. Akari reads sleep, heart rate and activity from Apple Health, so it works with any tracker that writes there, like an Apple Watch, an Oura Ring, a Garmin watch or a Fitbit. Turn on Apple Health in your tracker's own app, and keep the tracker you already have.

### Is Akari medical advice?

No. Akari explains your own data and patterns. It does not diagnose or treat anything, so talk to your doctor about health concerns.

### Does my health data leave my iPhone?

Your data stays private. Akari needs no account and keeps your health data on your iPhone. Only a food report you choose to send reaches Akari's server, so the team can fix the match. A meal you type, say or photograph is read by an AI service through Akari's server and not stored by Akari; details: https://joinakari.com/privacy/#meal-photos

### How can I try Akari?

Join the free beta through Apple TestFlight. The App Store version is coming soon.

## Brand assets

The brand page has every logo, the mark alone, the app icons and the colours, for each of the website's five themes: Shiratani (the default), Wasserkuppe, Loch Tay, Green River Overlook and Plain. All of them are in one ZIP: https://joinakari.com/brand/akari-brand.zip

Each file is also at https://joinakari.com/assets/brand/, named after its theme (shiratani, wasserkuppe, loch-tay, green-river-overlook or plain):

- akari-logo-<theme>-on-<dark|light>.svg and .png (2000 px wide): the mark above the wordmark, for a dark or a light background
- akari-mark-<theme>.svg and .png (1024 px wide): the mark alone
- akari-app-icon-<theme>-<light|dark>.png (1024 px): the app icon on its white or its black tile

For example, the plain logo for a light background is https://joinakari.com/assets/brand/akari-logo-plain-on-light.svg.
